Article Title: Nvidia H200 AI processors enter China: These two companies secure new batches
Article Text:
Infrastructure bottlenecks in Hong Kong

Chinese regulatory authorities have reportedly begun permitting limited quantities of Nvidia’s H200 artificial intelligence (AI) processors into mainland China, providing critical computing power to domestic tech companies as they work to close the technological gap with American competitors. Citing a source familiar with the developments, The Financial Times reported that both ByteDance and Tencent have taken delivery of roughly 10,000 H200 units over recent weeks while several others may receive clearance in the near future.The H200 processor sits at least two product cycles behind Nvidia’s flagship silicon, as strict US trade controls bar Chinese buyers from obtaining America's most capable AI hardware. Although export licenses issued by Washington allow individual Chinese organisations to acquire as many as 100,000 H200 units across both mainland China and Hong Kong, Beijing is directing companies to maintain the bulk of those purchases outside the mainland.The report says that this domestic policy is designed to protect and promote homegrown semiconductor alternatives. To balance these priorities, Chinese authorities have reportedly authorised tech firms to route H200 processors into Hong Kong, which functions outside mainland customs boundaries, and deploy them locally.Deploying high-performance hardware in Hong Kong, however, introduces logistical hurdles for Chinese technology companies. The region currently faces a deficit of data centre facilities capable of hosting large AI clusters, primarily driven by severe local power supply limitations that are unlikely to resolve quickly. Industry insiders note that while demand for the processors remains urgent, companies face significant obstacles utilising them efficiently in Hong Kong.Nvidia currently holds an inventory of roughly 500,000 H200 units set aside primarily for Chinese customers, though outbound deliveries had previously stalled under Beijing's regulatory limits.Hardware partners including Lenovo have recently notified Chinese enterprise clients that orders can resume for integrated AI servers built with H200 chips, CPUs, and enterprise networking hardware. However, domestic organisations must still clear a distinct review and authorization process managed by China’s primary economic planning body, the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC).
Article Summary: Beijing has allowed limited quantities of Nvidia’s H200 processors into mainland China. Both ByteDance and Tencent have taken delivery of roughly 10,000 H200 units over recent weeks while several others may receive clearance in the near future. H200 processor sits at least two product cycles behind Nvidia's flagship silicon.

Article Title: Google Pixel 11 Pro XL first impressions
Article Text:
Design and security

Performance

Gemini Intelligence now works ahead of you

Magic Capture for that perfect click

Camera Looks lets you choose your own style

Creator Suite simplifies content creation

Instant Night Sight speeds up low-light shots

Live Translate breaks language barriers instantly

What we think

Google’s newest flagship, the Pixel 11 Pro XL, has landed, and it comes packed with a fresh set of upgrades built around Gemini Intelligence and a reworked camera system that is supported by computational photography. From smarter photo sensors to an assistant that proactively steps in before you even ask, this year’s phone is clearly aimed at making everyday tasks simpler rather than bringing about notable changes in the hardware. Sure, the Pixel 11 Pro XL (price starting at Rs 1,34,999) packs improved security and processor upgrades, but those specs are tough to measure solely by benchmarks. Google’s true focus with this lineup is giving users a device that minimises screen time so you can actually focus on real life. Here's a look at everything that is new.The Pixel 11 Pro builds on Google’s refined aesthetic that has remained largely unchanged since the Pixel 9 Pro XL. The phone gets a brighter 6.8-inch Super Actua display than its predecessor. It features the same sleek, flat glass-and-metal sandwich design with Gorilla Glass Victus 2 and an IP68 rating. The phone retains the iconic horizontal rear camera bar, which has been cosmetically refined.The Pixel 11 Pro XL debuts HiLight, which works as an enhanced indicator light. Its functions are limited for now. The visor now has a full glass covering.The Pixel 11 Pro XL is powered by Tensor G6, which is claimed to offer better AI performance and handle daily tasks proactively. The phone gets a bunch of AI-driven features that are made possible by the new Tensor G6 chip, which handles the heavy lifting for on-device generative AI tasks like live dubbing and translation, letting the phone process complex features quickly without needing to lean entirely on the cloud. Add to that Titan M3, which adds a layer of intelligent security. Google says that the chip is capable of providing security from quantum attacks.The idea of the Pixel 11 Pro XL is not to perform well in raw benchmarks but to offer an experience that minimises human effort. For example, your friend recommends a restaurant that you also like. Now instead of searching for it and making a booking, Gemini will proactively offer you a reservation, which can be done in fewer taps. Here are a few AI features coming in the Pixel 11 Pro XL.The biggest shift with the Pixel 11 Pro XL is how much more capable Gemini has become at handling tasks on your behalf. It can now string together multiple steps across more than 40 apps and counting, and several of these abilities are debuting on Pixel before anywhere else.Google Pixel phones have been leaders for point-and-shoot photography, and with Gemini on Pixel 11 Pro, things are getting a bit easier. Magic Capture is built to catch those fleeting shots automatically that you may miss if you are a split second late.Not everyone loves the same photo aesthetic, and Camera Looks acknowledges this by allowing you to select your preferred style at the moment you take the shot. While the classic Pixel look remains a favourite for many, Google now offers three new default options: Natural, which keeps details relaxed; Shadows, which adds deeper contrast; and Vanilla, which brings a warm, golden tone. If you want to go further with personalisation, there are six additional Looks to choose from: Digi, Black Tie, Minimal, Editorial, Classic, and Velvet.For anyone who films content regularly, the new Creator Suite is designed to remove friction from the process. It brings an on-screen teleprompter that scrolls in sync with your speech, so you never lose your place while recording.If you have used Pixel smartphones in the past, you know how much time it takes for the phone to capture a shot in low-light condition. Google is fixing this by reducing time. Google says Night Sight shots can now be captured up to 4.5 times faster than before. During our time with the phone, it did speed up those times, helping us not to hold still for ages just to get a great low-light photo.Live Translate brings real-time translation to videos and audio as they play. It relies on real-time speech-to-speech translation, powered by advanced on-device generative AI models running on Google's Tensor G6 chip, automatically dubbing content from other languages into the one you prefer.Our early impressions are that Google Pixel 11 Pro XL has evolved into more of an experiential phone that offers a mix of great photography, clean software with straightforward design, and loads of AI features that aim to make day-to-day things easier for users over time. Tensor G6 still lags behind most of the flagship chipsets, but Google, like always, is aiming for a more software-centric approach rather than a hardware-led offering. We’ll talk about more in our full review.
Article Summary: Google’s newest flagship, the Pixel 11 Pro XL, has landed. It comes packed with a fresh set of upgrades built around Gemini Intelligence. From smarter photo sensors to an assistant that proactively steps in before you even ask, the phone is clearly aimed at making everyday tasks simpler rather than bringing about notable changes in the hardware.

Article Title: US tech company whose CEO fired 900 people in 79-second call tells court: Don't allow him to go to shareholders for 30 days
Article Text:
Vishal Garg made headlines in 2021 after he fired 900 employees over a video call

Why Better Home wants its former CEO Vishal Garg blocked

Vishal Garg wants his old job back

The 79-second Zoom call that made Vishal Garg ‘famous’

US-based Better Home & Finance has asked a US court to stop former CEO Vishal Garg from seeking shareholder support for at least 30 days, escalating a fight that began after the mortgage technology company removed him from the CEO role earlier this month. In a complaint filed in the US Southern District of New York, Better Home accused Garg of violating federal securities laws by allegedly seeking to build shareholder support to regain his job and making misleading statements. According to a report by Fortune, the company is also asking the court to cancel any shareholder approval Garg may have already collected.Better Home's board voted unanimously, excluding Vishal Garg, to remove him as CEO on August 3. The company then cited net losses of more than $1.5 billion since 2022 and a more than 90% fall in its stock price during Garg's tenure. After his removal, Garg launched what Better Home described in its complaint as a “campaign of retribution.”On August 10, Vishal Garg sent a letter to the company's board calling for the immediate resignation of all board members. He also said he had formed a “group of concerned shareholders” to help bring him back as CEO.In its complaint, Better Home alleges that Vishal Garg sought shareholder support through press releases, text messages, social media posts and an interview with Bloomberg. The company also claims Garg said he had “already corralled 52%” of the shareholder vote without filing the required proxy statements with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).Better Home is asking the court to prevent Garg from seeking shareholder support for at least 30 days and to void any shareholder approval he may have already obtained.As mentioned before, Vishal Garg was removed from the CEO position earlier this month after Daniel Lewis joined Better Home's board and was appointed CEO. Garg has since asked the board to reverse the decision and reinstate him. He has also offered to work for $1 a year until the company returns to profitability, after which he says he would step down.“It's an acknowledgement that I've been doing this for 10 years, but execution hasn't been perfect,” Garg said in an interview. “I hope it gets resolved. I think the future still remains very bright for Better.”Vishal Garg argues that his removal came as the company was working toward a potential turnaround. He also says that some investors contacted him after his ouster and wanted him to return.Vishal Garg is best known for a mass layoff in 2021, when he fired about 900 employees during a 79-second Zoom call. The incident drew widespread attention and damaged his reputation. Garg later described the employees as “lazy.” The company had previously said he was placed on leave following the mass layoffs.Garg was later reinstated as CEO in 2022 and was replaced this year.
Article Summary: Vishal Garg is best known for a mass layoff in 2021, when he fired about 900 employees during a 79-second Zoom call. The incident drew widespread attention and damaged his reputation. Vishal Garg was removed from the CEO position earlier this month after Daniel Lewis was appointed CEO.

Article Title: Sekyo Carepal Pro 2026 review: Safety, calling and GPS tracking in one watch
Article Text:
Display and design

Performance

Verdict

The Sekyo CarePro PAL 2026 is a kids' safety smartwatch (as the company calls it) that aims to combine communication, location tracking and safety features in one device. Listed at Rs 5,780 on the company’s website, it is positioned as more than a basic smartwatch, with features such as 4G calling, live GPS tracking, SOS alerts, Safe Zone notifications and parent-controlled monitoring. It also includes educational games and routine reminders for children. On paper, the CarePro PAL 2026 looks like a device designed to give parents more control while giving children some independence. But the real question is whether all these features work together well enough to make the Rs 5,880 price worthwhile in everyday use.Sekyo CarePro PAL 2026 has a design that feels clearly made for children rather than trying to look like a miniature version of an adult smartwatch. In our daily use, we found it comfortable enough for a child to wear throughout the day, while the compact form factor made it easy to use for calls, location checks and other basic functions.The watch also comes with a selfie camera, which adds to its practical appeal for children. We could use it for basic photos and video calling, while parents can access some of the camera-related features through the Sekyo app.The smartwatch has a 1.44-inch LCD display with a resolution of 240 x 240p.The display is primarily focused on usability rather than offering the kind of high-end screen experience we see on premium smartwatches. In our use, it was adequate for checking notifications, navigating the watch, making calls and accessing the games and other features. The touchscreen also makes it easier for children to interact with the device without relying on a smartphone.In our use, the 4G connectivity on the Sekyo CarePro PAL 2026 was central to the experience, as it allowed us to make HD video calls, phone calls and voice chats without giving the child a smartphone. Parents can also restrict communication to approved contacts, which adds an important layer of control.With Raksha Bandhan in mind, this is where the watch can also make sense as a gift from one sibling to another. Instead of being just another gadget, it can be a practical way for parents to stay connected with a younger brother or sister while allowing them some independence.We found the live GPS tracking to be one of the more useful features for parents. The Sekyo app can show the child's location, route history and step count. Parents can also create a Safe Zone, with an alert sent when the child moves outside the defined area.The SOS button adds another safety feature. A single press can share the child's live location and call up to three trusted contacts. For parents, this can provide an additional way to respond quickly when a child needs help.The watch also offers remote controls through the Sekyo app. We could enable school mode, block calls from unknown numbers, locate the watch and remotely disable or switch it off.The CarePro PAL 2026 comes with seven educational and maths games, along with an alarm, phone book and selfie camera. Routine reminders for activities such as brushing, homework, reading and bedtime can also help children follow a daily schedule.At Rs 5,880, the Sekyo CarePro PAL 2026 is aimed at parents who want to give a child some independence without handing over a smartphone. Its 4G calling, live GPS tracking, SOS alerts, Safe Zone notifications and parental controls make it more focused on safety and communication than typical kids' smartwatches. The educational games and habit reminders also give children something to use beyond calling and tracking. However, parents should remember that features such as GPS tracking and remote monitoring are dependent on connectivity and the companion app, so the overall experience can vary in real-world use.At Rs 5,880, the CarePro PAL 2026 makes the most sense for families that will actually use its safety and communication features. For a Raksha Bandhan gift, it offers a practical way to keep a younger brother or sister connected while giving parents greater peace of mind.
Article Summary: Sekyo CarePro PAL 2026 is a kids' safety smartwatch that aims to combine communication, location tracking and safety features in one device. It has features such as 4G calling, live GPS tracking, SOS alerts, Safe Zone notifications and parent-controlled monitoring. The smartwatch has a 1.44-inch LCD display with a resolution of 240 x 240p.

Article Title: ICE orders 'gadget ban' for its employees; says: You cannot come to work wearing...
Article Text:
US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)

Why ICE is treating Meta smart glasses like a body camera

Meta glasses keep showing up at immigration raids

Immigration and Customs Enforcement has told its employees to leave one particular gadget at home. In a memo issued on Tuesday, the agency barred staff from wearing Meta's smart glasses inside the federal workspace, treating the camera-equipped eyewear as a body-worn camera rather than a normal pair of Ray-Bans. The New York Times, which first reported the memo, said it was signed by acting director David Venturella.The worry is what the glasses can do without anyone around noticing. Venturella wrote that the devices could unintentionally capture, record or transmit sensitive information, potentially compromising privacy and legal protections. The restriction is not limited to officers working raids or arrests either. It applies to every ICE employee, desk staff included. Meta declined to comment to the Times.A Department of Homeland Security spokesman told the paper that personally owned body-worn cameras and unauthorised recording have always been off limits. That framing matters. It positions the memo less as a fresh policy and more as a reminder that an old one was being ignored.The hardware explains the nervousness. Meta's glasses carry a small camera above the frame that shoots video and audio, with a white LED that blinks while recording.Newer versions add a voice-controlled AI assistant and a tiny display tucked into the corner of one lens. Researchers have already shown the privacy LED can be worked around, which undercuts the one feature meant to warn bystanders.The memo lands after months of sightings. 404 Media reported in December that a Border Patrol agent in Charlotte, North Carolina wore Ray-Ban Metas during an operation with the recording light clearly lit. An activist who shared the photos described a flower vendor spotting agents and running into nearby woods, after which officers in bucket hats followed him in. One of them had the glasses on. CBP told 404 Media it has no arrangement with Meta, which points to agents buying the glasses themselves.An investigation by The Independent counted similar sightings across at least six states. Outside federal agencies, the pushback has been building too. New York became the first state to ban the glasses from its court buildings last month, and some restaurants and stores have shown wearers the door.None of this means the government has soured on the category itself. DHS asked for $7.5 million in its April budget proposal to build a smart glasses prototype of its own, including biometric identification features. So the objection is to consumer hardware in the field, not to face-scanning eyewear in principle.Meta, meanwhile, has made the glasses a pillar of its AI strategy, with Mark Zuckerberg calling them the ideal form of superintelligence. The company has kept an unreleased facial recognition feature under wraps, though the ACLU and 77 other groups asked it in April to abandon the idea entirely.
Article Summary: Immigration and Customs Enforcement has told its employees to leave one particular gadget at home. In a memo issued on Tuesday, the agency barred staff from wearing Meta's smart glasses inside the federal workspace. The worry is what the glasses can do without anyone around noticing. The restriction is not limited to officers working raids or arrests either.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Accenture CEO Julie Sweet: ‘We believe that transparency is needed to create trust, and…’; the workplace lesson behind her words
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Julie Sweet

“We believe that transparency is needed to create trust, and it's also needed to create a dialogue.”

What does Julie Sweet's quote mean

Why transparency can influence trust

Julie Sweet's career and leadership

Good leaders make room for honest responses

What the quote means for everyday work

What can be learned from Julie Sweet's quote

Explain decisions clearly: People understand change better when they know the reason behind it.

Be honest about uncertainty: Admitting that you do not have all the answers can build credibility.

Encourage questions: Transparency works best when people feel able to speak openly.

Accept disagreement: Trust does not mean everyone has to agree.

Listen as well as explain: Good dialogue allows leaders to learn from others.

Keep communication open: Trust grows when people are kept informed as situations change.

Trust at work environments is formed through little things, not through speeches. It may be formed through a manager who explains a rationale behind his or her decision, openness of a company regarding any problematic situations, or a leader who admits that there are some issues which have not been resolved yet. People are not expected to agree with everything, but people normally need to be informed of what is going on and why it is going on. Lack of information creates uncertainty, and the process of acceptance of any changes becomes more complicated.It is not simply about sharing information. It is also about creating enough openness for people to ask questions, raise concerns and take part in a conversation. This kind of openness can make difficult conversations easier, reduce confusion, encourage honest feedback and help employees feel more secure during periods of change. Julie Sweet, chair and chief executive of Accenture, has expressed this idea in a simple observation.In simple terms, Sweet is saying that people are more likely to trust an organisation when they feel they are being kept informed.Transparency does not mean that everyone will agree with a decision. It does not guarantee that difficult news will become easier to hear either.What it can do is reduce uncertainty.Imagine a company changing its working arrangements. Employees may not like the new policy, but knowing why it was introduced, how it will affect them and where they can raise concerns gives them a clearer basis for responding. That is where the second part of Sweet's quote becomes important. Transparency can turn an announcement into a conversation.Trust tends to develop over time. It is built through repeated experiences of how people communicate, particularly when circumstances are difficult.If employees are regularly given information only after decisions have already been made, they may begin to feel disconnected from the process. By contrast, explaining what is known, what is changing and what remains uncertain can give people a better understanding of where they stand.There is no guarantee that this will remove disagreement. In fact, openness can sometimes lead to more questions. But questions are part of the dialogue Sweet refers to.A workplace where people can ask why something happened is different from one where information simply moves from senior management downwards.There is also a practical limit to openness. Companies deal with confidential information, legal matters, personal data and commercial decisions that cannot always be discussed publicly. Being transparent does not mean removing every boundary around information.Instead, it can mean explaining what can be shared and, where appropriate, why some details cannot yet be disclosed.That distinction matters because unrealistic expectations can make transparency difficult to maintain. People may not need every internal detail. They usually need enough context to understand the decisions that affect them.Sweet's perspective comes from a career that began in law rather than technology.She joined Accenture in 2010 after working as a partner at the law firm Cravath, Swaine & Moore. At Accenture, she initially held senior legal and compliance responsibilities before moving into broader business leadership. She became chief executive in 2019 and chair in 2021.Her rise also involved learning outside her original area of expertise. When she joined Accenture, she spoke about needing to strengthen her understanding of technology and relying on colleagues to help her learn.That experience fits with a wider point about leadership. Credibility does not necessarily come from appearing to have every answer. Sometimes it comes from being willing to ask questions and acknowledge what still needs to be understood.The word “dialogue” gives Sweet's quote another layer. Communication can be one-way. A leader can issue a statement, employees can read it and the process can end there.The dialogue is different. It allows information to move in both directions. An employee may notice a problem that senior management has missed. A customer may raise an issue that changes how a product is developed. A team working in another part of the world may see the consequences of a decision differently.Those responses can be uncomfortable, but they can also provide information that would otherwise remain hidden.Transparency, in this sense, is not simply about explaining decisions. It is about making space for people to respond to them.Sweet's words do not apply only to chief executives or large corporations.A manager changing a deadline, a team leader introducing a new process or a business owner dealing with a difficult period can face the same basic issue.A short explanation can sometimes make a significant difference. Instead of simply saying that a deadline has moved, a manager might explain what caused the change. Instead of announcing a new procedure without context, a team could be told what problem it is intended to solve.These are small examples, but they reflect the same principle.People generally handle uncertainty better when they have some idea of what is happening.
Article Summary: Julie Sweet, chair and chief executive of Accenture, has expressed this idea in a simple observation. In simple terms, Sweet is saying that people are more likely to trust an organisation when they feel they are being kept informed. It is also about creating enough openness for people to ask questions, raise concerns and take part in a conversation.

Article Title: CRED launches 'Circle by CRED' in Beta, a mentorship network for members
Article Text:
CRED

CRED leverages affluent peer network

Rollout and access

Fintech platform CRED has announced the beta rollout of Circle by CRED, a standalone application designed to facilitate direct, one-on-one advisory sessions between CRED members and domain specialists across careers, financial decisions, wellness, and personal relationships.The platform addresses what the company calls a scarcity of earned judgment amid modern information overload. During the beta phase, select members can connect directly with over 100 vetted "Residents"—experienced industry operators and subject experts drawn from the platform's wider network.Circle by CRED taps into the company’s base of 1.7 crore members. The initiative aims to offer members fresh strategic perspectives and accelerate decision-making across personal and professional domains. Residents on the platform serve as active thought partners.Seasoned founders provide guidance on capital raising and leadership recruitment for early-stage entrepreneurs while product executives and senior leaders assist members navigating major career pivots. Similarly lifestyle and relationships specialists provide actionable feedback on dating profiles and interpersonal matters.Residents undergo a curation process based on their operational background, verified credentials, and subject-matter relevance.Members can consult Residents via text messaging, audio calls, or video sessions, which are open daily from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM IST throughout the week.Pricing Structure: Consultation rates start at Rs 25 per minute, allowing for single quick inquiries or recurring sessions for multi-step discussions.Commenting on the launch, Miten Sampat, interim CEO of CRED, said: "Information and intelligence are abundant now, but judgement and taste are still developed through experience. For our affluent members, the collective experience of qualified peers is now a conversation away, with a high-signal network on Circle by CRED to enable their progress."While Circle by CRED is currently accessible in beta to a select user group, the company plans to introduce additional categories and scale the network over time.CRED members can download the app on iOS and Android to join the waitlist, while individuals interested in joining the roster of advisory Residents can submit applications directly at cred.club/residents.
Article Summary: CRED launches Circle by CRED, a one-on-one advisory service for its 1.7 crore members. Members can connect directly with over 100 vetted "Residents"—experienced industry operators and subject experts. Residents undergo a curation process based on their operational background, verified credentials, and subject-matter relevance.

Article Title: Navi raises USD 100 million from Prosus: Sachin Bansal's fintech takes its first institutional cheque
Article Text: Navi Limited has announced a USD 100 million investment from Prosus, the first time Sachin Bansal's financial services group has taken institutional capital since he started building it. The deal is still subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory clearances, including approval from the Competition Commission of India.The timing matters more than the number. Navi has spent years running on Bansal's own money, an unusual position for a company operating in lending and payments, where balance sheet depth is the whole game. Bringing in an outside investor at this stage signals a shift from a self-funded experiment to something Navi wants treated as an institution.Bansal's association with Naspers and the Prosus Group goes back more than a decade, dating to the Flipkart years, and both sides referenced that history in announcing the deal. Bansal called Prosus one of the world's most respected investors and said the value goes beyond the cheque, pointing to its global perspective and experience scaling technology businesses.Ashutosh Sharma, head of Prosus India investments and M&A, said Navi ticked the boxes the firm looks for: a large loyal user base, multiple business lines on one platform, a technology-first approach and a focus on consumer experience.He specifically credited the team's execution over the past 12 months in what he described as a tough macro environment, and said Bansal shares the firm's philosophy of patient company-building.The operating numbers give the investment some grounding. Navi UPI held its position as India's fourth-largest UPI app through FY26, which is no small thing in a market where PhonePe and Google Pay control most of the volume. Navi Finserv pushed its lending AUM past ₹130 billion. The group turned consolidated profitable in Q4 FY26, helped by improving unit economics and operating leverage.That combination, scale in payments and profitability in lending, is what Prosus appears to be buying into ahead of the next phase.
Article Summary: Navi Limited announced a USD 100 million investment from Prosus. It is the first time Sachin Bansal's financial services group has taken institutional capital since he started building it. The deal is still subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory clearances, including approval from the Competition Commission of India.

Article Title: Fujifilm opens India’s first House of Photography in Mumbai with cameras, creator experiences and more
Article Text:
"Through Fujifilm House of Photography, we are bringing our global vision of creating spaces that go beyond showcasing products to fostering creativity, learning and community. India is one of the world's most dynamic and creative markets, and we are delighted to introduce this concept here as part of our long-term commitment to nurturing the country's evolving imaging ambitions."

Fujifilm House of Photography brings cameras and imaging solutions

Mumbai House of Photography includes creator studio and workshops

“We are delighted to bring Fujifilm House of Photography to India and create a space dedicated to photographers, creators and visual storytellers of every generation. At Fujifilm, our Group Purpose of 'Giving our world more smiles' inspires us to create experiences that enrich people's lives, and we hope this House of Photography becomes a welcoming destination where creativity is nurtured, memories are preserved and stories are shared.

"

Fujifilm India has opened its first Fujifilm House of Photography in the country in Mumbai. With this, the company is bringing cameras, printing solutions, workshops and creator-focused facilities under one roof. Located in Andheri West, the two-storey, 5,795 sq. ft. destination opened on August 19, World Photography Day.The Mumbai facility is Fujifilm's eleventh House of Photography globally and features hands-on experiences with the company's instax, X Series and GFX System cameras, along with QuickSnap cameras, binoculars and printing solutions. It also includes a creator studio, photo gallery, workshop area and Pro Print Centre.Mr Yujiro Igarashi, General Manager, Imaging Business Division, said,The ground floor of the Mumbai House of Photography is dedicated to product experiences. Visitors can explore the instax, X Series and GFX System through guided demonstrations, along with dedicated areas for QuickSnap single-use cameras and binoculars.The space includes a live instax print bar, an X Series discovery table and a GFX and lens display. Fujifilm has also introduced a dedicated experience zone for its Z Series projectors, marking the first time the company is showcasing the projector lineup through such a space in India.Visitors can also explore Fujifilm's printing solutions and see how digital photographs can be converted into physical prints.The first floor has been designed as a community and creative space, featuring a photo gallery, creator studio and workshop area. It also includes a Pro Print Centre and dedicated enterprise imaging solutions.The company plans to use the space for workshops, exhibitions, creator meet-ups and photo walks. These activities are intended to give photographers, filmmakers, content creators, and other visitors opportunities to learn and collaborate.Mr. Koji Wada, Managing Director, Fujifilm India, said,The interior design draws on India's architectural heritage, combining traditional design elements with Art Deco influences. The facility is located at Chandak Unicorn in Andheri West and covers approximately 5,795 sq. ft. across two levels.The opening comes in a year marking 200 years since the invention of photography. Fujifilm said the House of Photography is intended to provide an end-to-end imaging experience spanning product exploration, learning, creation, printing and community activities.
Article Summary: Mumbai House of Photography includes creator studio and workshops. Located in Andheri West, the two-storey, 5,795 sq. ft. destination opened on August 19, World Photography Day. It features hands-on experiences with the company's instax, X Series and GFX System cameras, along with QuickSnap cameras and binoculars.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Nikesh Arora: ‘Always be learning’
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora

Don't read long form books my friend. I guzzle information, I absorb from wherever I can. I have read as much about

agentic architectures

lately to build a mental teamwork to understand how one might protect our customers in such a future.

Always be learning

. Many long form books take a lot of prose to make a few points, I find summaries interesting there, unless I feel like a good story.

What Nikesh Arora’s quote means

A message reflected in his approach

Nikesh Arora does not fit the mould of the traditional bookish tech executive who may have sworn by finishing every book cover to cover before forming an opinion. As the Chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks, one of the world's leading cybersecurity companies, Arora has built his approach to leadership around a very different philosophy: one focused less on ritual and more on relentless intake. This quote captures that mindset in just three words and it says a lot more than it appears to at first glance.On the surface, this sounds like standard leadership advice. But Arora's own description of how he actually learns gives the phrase real weight. He has been candid that he isn't someone who sits down with long-form books in the traditional sense. Instead, he describes himself as someone who “guzzles” information, absorbing it from wherever he can find it, whenever he can find it.This distinction matters. “Always be learning” is a description of an ongoing, almost restless state of curiosity, one that doesn't wait for a scheduled reading hour or a curated syllabus. For Arora, learning is a continuous background process, running in parallel with everything else he does as a CEO.He has pointed to his recent deep dive into agentic architectures as a concrete example of this in action. Rather than treating it as an abstract technology trend to observe from a distance, Arora has said he's read extensively on the subject specifically to build what he calls a “mental teamwork,” an internal framework for understanding how his company might protect its customers as agentic systems become more central to how businesses operate.That's learning with an explicit, applied purpose, not learning as a passive intellectual exercise.Arora has also been fairly direct about his relationship with long-form books specifically. He has noted that many of them stretch a handful of core ideas across hundreds of pages, and that he often finds more value in summaries that get straight to the point, unless a book happens to offer something he genuinely wants to experience as a story.
Article Summary: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora says he 'guzzles' information. He doesn't read long-form books, he reads summaries unless he feels like a good story. For Arora, learning is a continuous background process, running in parallel with everything else he does as a CEO.

Article Title: Planning to buy Samsung’s foldable smartphone, why the best time is right now
Article Text:
Why analyst are forecasting a price hike

Double-digit growth in uber-premium segment to help foldable sales

Pre-orders and discounts: What the numbers tell

Most of the phone shoppers know the drill: wait for a big sale to get a better deal on your purchase. However, this year may be different as that old logic doesn’t hold. This is due to the rising prices of one of the main components of a smartphone: RAM, which has already resulted in increasing the prices of phones. Foldable smartphones are the ones that sit on the top of the pack in terms of price. If you have your eye on one of the recently-launched Samsung foldables: Do not wait is what analysts and retailers say. The reason is likely price hike of foldable phones across the board.According to leading retailers in the country, Samsung’s new foldable smartphones Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Galaxy Z Fold8 and Galaxy Z Flip8 are set to become costlier in India as soon as in the next month. Priced between Rs 1.25 lakh and Rs 2.6 lakh, the new Samsung foldables offer a refined foldable experience by combining purpose-built Galaxy AI with engineering across hinge design, display, durability and performance. For example, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra measures 4.1mm when unfolded, and is the thinnest Galaxy Z Fold yet. On the other hand, Galaxy Z Fold8 weighs 201 grams, making it Samsung’s lightest Fold yet.Analysts say Samsung increasing the prices of its new Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Galaxy Z Fold8 and Galaxy Z Flip8 smartphones in India is coming and will not be surprising. Counterpoint Research’s numbers show that DRAM and NAND prices are expected to increase by another 30% between Q2 2026 and Q4 2026 after an 85% hike in Q1 further raising costs for foldable devices, which typically feature higher RAM and storage configurations.Notably, DRAM and NAND contribute to around 27% of the BoM in foldables Unlike conventional smartphones, foldables also carry additional costs associated with flexible displays, sophisticated hinge mechanisms, reinforced structural components and more complex manufacturing processes.According to Tarun Pathak, research director at Counterpoint Research, not just RAM but SoC are also going to drive the costs up. The recent price increase in memory and semiconductors stems from the dramatic rise of the AI industry. A growing number of companies are designing proprietary silicon, placing severe strain on global supply chains and fabrication capacity. He said that the research company sees no signs of memory prices going down at least for the next two years.“With no clear peak for memory pricing in sight, brands need to take preemptive action. Even foldable devices – which typically have enough margin depth to absorb cost pressures – are vulnerable to this uncertainty, likely forcing OEMs to make tough choices,” he told The Times of India.Meanwhile, Abhilash Kumar, lead research advisor (Director) at Smart Analytics Global (SAG) said that the smartphone market in India will continue to see annual shipment decline in Q3 and Q4 2026, given the global memory shortage in the smartphone industry leading to prices increase.“Prices of some smartphones already retailing in the market have been going up, and new smartphones could launch with a costlier price tag. The rising prices are certain to impact the upcoming festive season sales volumes in India and overall, we might not see discounts as attractive as we witnessed in past couple of years,” added Kumar.According to Prabhu Ram, vice president, Industry Research Group at CMR, CyberMedia Research found that India’s premium smartphone segment continues to deliver double-digit growth, underscoring the strength of demand among the country’s increasingly aspirational consumers. Against this backdrop, the eighth-generation foldables are well positioned to benefit from sustained interest in the uber-premium segment.“However, the RAMageddon realities loom large for consumers eyeing their next upgrade. With DRAM and NAND prices remaining elevated, premium smartphones with higher memory and storage configurations could face further price pressure in the coming months, potentially making the next upgrade more expensive for consumers,” Ram added.Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Galaxy Z Fold8 and Galaxy Z Flip8 secured record pre-orders in India, with nearly 2.71 lakh consumers pre-ordering these smartphones within just 72 hours of their launch, according to Samsung India. The devices opened to sales earlier this month, but retailers fear a price hike may be around the corner given the rising demand for memory chips that are a vital component for smartphones.Samsung last month said that it has been absorbing the incremental cost of smartphones to a great extent keeping the consumers’ interest in mind. The company has also launched a long tenure zero-cost EMI for Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Galaxy Z Fold8 and Galaxy Z Flip8 buyers in India.“If you compare how much they (competition) have increased the price, Samsung's increment is relatively lesser than competition because we have been absorbing the cost. Not because we want to maintain the market share or grow the market share, but as a company that is focussed to provide the best devices, the loss that we are taking in 2026 is humongous,” JB Park, president and CEO of Samsung Southwest Asia said in London at the launch of the new Galaxy foldables.
Article Summary: Samsung’s new foldable smartphones are set to become costlier in India as soon as in the next month. The reason is likely price hike of foldable phones across the board. DRAM and NAND prices are expected to increase by another 30% between Q2 2026 and Q4 2026 after an 85% hike in Q1.

Article Title: AWS announces new builder lofts in three global tech hubs
Article Text:
Why three cities

AWS has announced plans to open new Builder Lofts in Berlin, Hyderabad, and São Paulo. These permanent spaces will provide free workshops, networking events, pitch nights, content creation areas, and co‑working opportunities for developers, students, and tech professionals. In the early days of cloud computing, AWS supported builders through Pop‑up Lofts worldwide. More recently, Gen AI Lofts offered collaborative spaces focused on generative AI. Recognizing the need for permanent community hubs, AWS opened its first Builder Loft in San Francisco in July 2025, which has since welcomed more than 22,500 developers through hackathons, demo nights, and workshops.* Berlin: Following the launch of AWS European Sovereign Cloud, the Berlin Loft will host sessions on digital sovereignty, hackathons, and security workshops, connecting Germany’s startup ecosystem with Europe’s broader tech landscape.* Hyderabad: The Loft will give Indian developers a dedicated space to upskill on AI, explore cloud‑native architecture, and collaborate on next‑generation applications.* São Paulo: With Brazil’s cloud market growing at 30% annually, the Loft will serve as a hub for Latin America’s developers, offering programming in partnership with local communities, universities, and startups.The Builder Lofts are designed to be flexible, transforming from training rooms to demo stages or meetup venues.Programming is shaped by local developers, user groups, and tech leaders, while AWS provides the space, infrastructure, and support.AWS will announce opening dates for the new Builder Lofts in future updates. To learn more and follow along, visit the AWS Builder Loft page."Twenty years ago, AWS launched its first services, and it was the builder community that believed in us from the very beginning," said David Nalley, director of developer experience at AWS. "These spaces are our way of investing back into that community, giving developers a place to come together, build real things, and learn from each other. Not through a screen, but in person, side by side."
Article Summary: AWS will open new Builder Lofts in Berlin, Hyderabad, and São Paulo. These permanent spaces will provide free workshops, networking events, pitch nights, content creation areas, and co‑working opportunities for developers, students, and tech professionals. AWS opened its first Builder Loft in San Francisco in July 2025.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos makes his first foray into sports ownership, with his consortium taking close to 40% stake in Liverpool
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos enters sports ownership with Liverpool deal

FSG remains in control

Jeff Bezos has entered sports ownership for the first time after joining a consortium that has bought about a 40% stake in Liverpool Football Club. The consortium, called 1892 Holdings, is led by former Queens Park Rangers co-owner Amit Bhatia and also includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin’s family office, and the Mittal Family Trusts. The deal gives the group a significant minority stake in the Premier League club, while Fenway Sports Group (FSG) will remain Liverpool’s majority owner and retain operational control. The agreement also includes an option that could allow the consortium to buy a controlling stake in Liverpool within the next 12 months.Jeff Bezos’ investment in Liverpool comes through K5 Sports and marks his first move into sports ownership. However, Bezos will not have a seat on Liverpool’s board. Bryan Baum from K5 Sports and Elaine Saverin will join Amit Bhatia on the board, according to the details of the deal. Bhatia will also serve as vice-chairman of Liverpool after the investment.The consortium's stake is larger than earlier estimates. Initial reports had suggested that the group had bought between about 30% and one-third of the club. The stake is now understood to be closer to 40%, at around 38%, according to people familiar with the deal.Despite the investment, FSG will continue to be Liverpool's majority shareholder and will retain control over the club's operations. FSG said the investment is intended to support Liverpool's long-term growth.“The strategic investment supports Liverpool FC’s long-term growth ambitions by bringing together experts from across global business, technology and investment,” FSG said in a statement. The company added that the new consortium partners will work with FSG and Liverpool's leadership team to explore opportunities for the club both on and off the pitch.“FSG continues to retain majority ownership and operational control of Liverpool FC,” the company said.The agreement also gives 1892 Holdings a mechanism to potentially buy a controlling stake in Liverpool over the next 12 months. However, the option is not a formal commitment to make the purchase. It gives the consortium the opportunity to increase its ownership if the terms of the agreement are met.Bhatia said the group was proud to invest in Liverpool alongside FSG.“We are incredibly proud to be investing in Liverpool Football Club and to be doing so alongside FSG,” he said. “To be welcomed as a partner in a club of this stature is a huge privilege. We are making this investment because we believe deeply in Liverpool and its leadership, and we look forward to supporting the club’s continued success for years to come.”
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos has joined a consortium that has bought a 40% stake in Liverpool Football Club. The consortium, called 1892 Holdings, is led by former Queens Park Rangers co-owner Amit Bhatia. It also includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin’s family office, and the Mittal Family Trusts. The deal gives the group a significant minority stake in the club.

Article Title: American billionaire Mark Cuban 'warns' Senator Ro Khanna, say that only idiot startup founders will stay in California if his bill is passed
Article Text:
Mark Cuban’s argument

Threat to California’s startup ecosystem

Read Mark Cuban’s complete post here

Ro, I like you. You know that. But you need to read the state of the state.

The number of Deca Unicorns in Cali is growing by the day as investors chase amazing startups.

A unique feature of these 10b startups is that even if they raise a billion, little, if any of that money goes to the founders, who are now worth billions of dollars over night. They are the definition of cash poor, stock rich

How are you going to tax them ? Make them borrow money against their shares, if they can? They just raised money to grow their company and a bank will come along and loan them money ? A company that has been in business maybe less than a year ? lol

Will you take their stock if they can’t ?

Do you really think each of multiple founders, who started an amazing company in Cali and is now a billionaire, can each just pull out $250m per billion of net worth from their raise ? You know they can’t.

If this passes , and it doesn’t directly impact me at all, I won’t be a cali resident, but you can bet if I’m investing in a multi billion dollar startup, I’m asking them to move from California first.

IMO, if this passes, only idiot startup founders stay in Cali.

I’ve done it before and will do it again. Dallas. Pittsburgh. Indiana. I will make NOT being in California a pre requisite for an investment

Ideology is not a strategy Ro.

American billionaire Mark Cuban has issued a sharp warning to Representative Ro Khanna (D‑Calif.) over California’s proposed 5% billionaire tax, known as Proposition 40. In a lengthy post shared on social media platform X (Formerly known as Twitter) Cuban argued that the measure would drive startup founders out of the state, saying blunt that ‘only idiot startup founders’ would remain if the bill passes. The tax proposal, set for a vote on November 3, would levy 5% on all assets owned by California’s wealthiest residents to fund healthcare, schools, and food assistance programs. Supporters, including Khanna, frame it as standing up for the working class against the billionaire elite amid rising living costs. Cuban, however, warned that the policy misunderstands how startup wealth works.Cuban explained that many founders of “Deca Unicorns” — startups valued at $10 billion or more — are cash poor but stock rich. Their net worth comes from equity, not liquid assets. Taxing them would force founders to borrow against shares or sell stock prematurely, undermining growth. “Do you really think each of multiple founders can just pull out $250 million per billion of net worth from their raise? You know they can’t,” he wrote.Cuban said if the measure passes, he would make not being in California a prerequisite for investment, citing Dallas, Pittsburgh, and Indiana as alternatives.He warned that the tax would accelerate capital flight and discourage innovation in Silicon Valley. “Ideology is not a strategy, Ro,” Cuban added, stressing that the bill risks dismantling California’s startup advantage.
Article Summary: Cuban said he would make not being in California a prerequisite for investment. He warned that the tax would accelerate capital flight and discourage innovation in Silicon Valley. The tax proposal, set for a vote on November 3, would levy 5% on all assets owned by California's wealthiest residents.

Article Title: Discord suspends livestreams in Brazil after criticism over child safety and a 13-year-old's suicide
Article Text:

“We remain committed to working with public policymakers in Brazil to help create an online experience that is safer for all, on Discord and across the internet.”

Discord livestreams suspended after Brazil child safety case

Discord complaints rise in Brazil

Brazil tightens internet rules for minors

Discord has suspended its livestreaming features in Brazil. This comes after criticism over child safety on the platform and a case involving the death of a 13-year-old girl. The decision came after Brazil’s national data protection agency ordered the company to suspend the livestreaming features last week, citing concerns about risks to children and adolescents.In a statement to AP, the live streaming site said it is in discussions with Brazilian authoritiesDiscord also said,The action follows a case in July involving an underage girl in Mato Grosso do Sul who was allegedly coerced by other users into committing suicide during a livestream on Discord. Five teenagers were arrested in connection with the death, according to an August 4 statement from Brazil’s justice ministry. Brazil’s first lady Rosângela Lula da Silva, known as Janja, called for Discord to be taken offline after the incident.said Janja at a ceremony in Brasilia on August 6.Brazil’s national data protection agency said livestreams had been used to facilitate violence, harassment and the incitement of self-harm and suicide.The agency also said there was evidence that Discord had not sufficiently prevented children and adolescents from being exposed to content involving violence, self-harm and suicide.Discord said it had investigated a private server where people involved in criminal activity were believed to have encouraged self-harm. The company said it shut down the server before the 13-year-old’s death and denied that the incident was shown live on its platform.The company said groups or individuals promoting violence have no place on Discord and that its safety teams work to remove violating content and take action against accounts involved in harmful activity.Discord has more than 90 million daily active users worldwide, according to the company’s website. In Brazil, complaints involving Discord increased by 54% between January and July compared with the same period last year, according to data from internet rights nonprofit Safernet Brazil.Thiago Tavares, president of Safernet Brazil, said the case involving the 13-year-old was part of a wider pattern of concerns involving the platform.Tavares said in a statement on August 11.He also said Brazil’s digital law establishesand that failure to comply should result in accountability.Thiago Ayub, director of technology at network engineering company Sage Networks, criticised the decision to suspend the livestreaming feature. He argued that users involved in criminal activity could move to other platforms that are not facing the same level of scrutiny.Ayub said.Brazil has introduced regulations to increase protections for minors online. Under the rules, children under 16 must link their social media accounts to a legal guardian, and digital services must implement age verification measures beyond simply asking users to declare they are over 18.Discord postponed an age verification policy in February following criticism from users concerned about privacy. The company later said it was introducing age assurance measures to comply with Brazilian regulations.The Discord decision comes amid broader efforts by Brazil’s government and Supreme Court to regulate how minors use online services. Other countries, including Australia, Canada and Indonesia, have also introduced or considered measures aimed at addressing online risks to children.The Trump administration has accused Brazil of targeting US social media companies and has cited the issue as one reason for imposing tariffs on Brazilian imports. In 2024, Brazil’s Supreme Court ordered the suspension of X in the country until the platform complied with orders to remove accounts spreading disinformation.
Article Summary: Discord has suspended its livestreaming features in Brazil. This comes after criticism over child safety on the platform and a case involving the death of a 13-year-old girl. In Brazil, complaints involving Discord increased by 54% between January and July compared with the same period last year. Brazil has introduced regulations to increase protections for minors online.

Article Title: Quote of the Day by Thomas Alva Edison: Genius is one per cent inspiration, ninety-nine per cent...
Article Text:
Thomas Alva Edison held more than 1,000 patents and built the world's first industrial research lab.

The ratio kept changing before it settled at 1 and 99

Edison was not the first person to make the point

Nikola Tesla thought the approach was the problem, not the virtue

Why the line still lands in 2026

"Genius is one per cent inspiration, ninety-nine per cent perspiration." It is the line that launched a million motivational posters, and it belongs to Thomas Alva Edison, the man who turned invention into an industrial process. The sentiment is simple enough. Ideas are cheap and abundant. What separates a working phonograph from a sketch on a napkin is the grinding, unglamorous middle stretch that nobody photographs.What makes the quote more interesting than the poster version suggests is that Edison's claim to it has been picked apart for decades. The best known citation is a September 1932 article in Harper's Monthly, written by Martin Andre Rosanoff, a chemist who had worked in Edison's laboratory, in which Edison takes credit for the saying himself. He had also claimed authorship in a 1927 letter, writing that he had indeed made the statement and still held the same opinion.Edison was clearly circling the idea for years before it crystallised into its famous form. The Ladies' Home Journal ran a version in April 1898 in which he put the split at two per cent genius and ninety-eight per cent hard work. Scientific American carried the same 2:98 ratio in December 1902.The now familiar 1:99 wording was being attributed to him by 1901.Quote researchers have found the underlying idea in circulation before Edison was credited with it, including a speech by a shoe company president to high school students in May 1898. Forbes has pointed to Kate Sanborn, an academic who lectured on the question of what genius is during the early 1890s and defined it as a blend of inspiration and perspiration, though no ratio of hers was recorded. Edison's contribution, arguably, was compression. He gave a diffuse idea a number and a rhythm.The most enjoyable counterpoint came from inside the industry. Tesla, who worked for Edison briefly, later described his old employer's method as searching a haystack straw by straw, and said a little theory and calculation would have spared him most of the labour. Two centuries of R&D philosophy sit in that exchange. Edison ran trials until something worked. Tesla wanted to think his way to the answer first.The quote has found a second life in the AI era, where prompts are free and prototypes take an afternoon. The one per cent has never been more accessible. The ninety-nine per cent, the testing, the shipping, the fixing of what breaks at scale, remains exactly as expensive as it was when Edison was burning through filament materials in Menlo Park.
Article Summary: Edison was not the first person to make the point. Nikola Tesla thought the approach was the problem, not the virtue. The quote has found a second life in the AI era, where prompts are free and prototypes take an afternoon. The ninety- nine per cent, the testing, the shipping, the fixing of what breaks at scale, remains exactly as expensive as it was when Edison was burning through filament materials.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Bill Gates: "We all need people who will give us feedback. That's how we…" - a lesson on honest feedback, blind spots and the real work of getting better
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Bill Gates

Quote of the day by Bill Gates

"We all need people who will give us feedback. That's how we improve"

The real story behind this quote

Understand the meaning behind the quote by Bill Gates

Why feedback is genuinely different from simple praise

Why this quote matters even more today

We all have genuine blind spots

Real improvement requires genuine honesty

Not every single opinion needs to be followed

Good feedback should genuinely lead to action

Other memorable quotes by Bill Gates

"It's fine to celebrate success but it is more important to heed the lessons of failure."

"Your most unhappy customers are your greatest source of learning."

"If you can't make it good, at least make it look good."

"Success is a lousy teacher. It seduces smart people into thinking they can't lose."

How to actually apply this quote in daily life

Final takeaway from this quote

Feedback can be genuinely uncomfortable, particularly when it points directly at something we would rather not notice about ourselves. A colleague might question an idea at work. A teacher might point out a real weakness in an assignment. The first instinct is not always to actually listen either. Sometimes it is simply to explain, to defend, or to quietly move on instead. Bill Gates , the Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist, made a simple but genuinely useful point about exactly this. "We all need people who will give us feedback. That's how we improve," he said, during a TED talk specifically focused on improving the quality of education. He continued by pointing out something genuinely striking, that when he and Melinda first learned how little useful feedback most teachers actually received, they were "blown away. " Until fairly recently, over 98 per cent of teachers received precisely one word of feedback throughout their entire career, "satisfactory."Gates made this point in far richer detail than the single sentence usually shared alone."If all my bridge coach ever told me was that I was 'satisfactory,' I would have no hope of ever getting better," he told his TED audience. "How would I know who was the best? How would I know what I was doing differently?" He then pointed directly to Shanghai, a province in China widely recognised for producing genuinely strong educational outcomes, describing exactly how its system actually worked in practice. "They made sure that younger teachers get a chance to watch master teachers at work," he explained. "They have weekly study groups, where teachers get together and talk about what's working. They even require each teacher to observe and give feedback to their colleagues." That real, specific example gives the quote considerably more weight than a vague general statement about the value of feedback ever could on its own.The quote itself is genuinely straightforward. Gates is saying that real improvement requires some kind of outside perspective, because people naturally develop blind spots they simply cannot see on their own. Someone might genuinely believe they communicate clearly, right up until a colleague tells them their instructions actually came across as confusing. A manager might think they are already giving their team enough support, only to discover that their employees genuinely see the situation quite differently. Feedback is what brings that missing perspective properly into view. None of this means every single piece of criticism is automatically correct, and it does not mean people should simply accept every opinion offered to them without thinking it through first. Useful feedback genuinely needs to be considered carefully, questioned where necessary, and acted upon only when it actually makes sense to do so.The word feedback can sound fairly formal, yet the actual idea behind it is part of completely ordinary life. Parents give feedback to their children constantly. Teachers give it to students. Colleagues give it to each other, often without ever using the word itself directly. There is also a real difference between feedback and simple praise worth being clear about. Praise can genuinely be encouraging, but feedback becomes especially useful the moment it actually contains something a person can genuinely learn from. A writer might be told an article was interesting, which feels nice, but it is genuinely more useful to know exactly which section was unclear, and why it read that way. Gates' entire point is really that people need honest responses from others if they actually want a clearer picture of their own work and behaviour, rather than simply more approval.The genuine need for real feedback has become considerably more visible as people work, learn and communicate in increasingly different ways from before. Many employees now work with teams they may never actually see in person. Businesses constantly collect customer reviews and detailed performance data. There is genuinely no shortage of raw information available anywhere. The real challenge lies in knowing what to actually do with all of it. Online reactions in particular can be genuinely complicated to interpret properly, since a large volume of comments does not automatically mean the feedback itself is actually useful. Good feedback works differently. It gives a person something genuinely concrete to actually consider and act on.Nobody sees their own behaviour from every possible angle at once. A person knows exactly what they intended to say, while other people only ever experience what was actually said out loud. That gap between intention and impact can genuinely matter, and feedback is really what helps close it properly.Useful feedback is not always flattering to hear, and sometimes the information that actually helps the most is precisely the information that is genuinely difficult to sit with. Someone willing to listen to an uncomfortable observation has considerably more useful information to work with than someone who only ever seeks simple approval from the people around them.Listening carefully to feedback was never the same thing as agreeing with absolutely everything you hear. Feedback comes from real individuals with their own genuine experiences, expectations and biases attached to it. It makes sense to actually consider the source, look for genuine patterns across multiple people, and decide honestly whether the criticism is actually supported by real evidence.Feedback has fairly limited value if it simply ends with a single conversation and nothing else. The genuinely useful part comes once a person actually takes what they have learned and makes a real change because of it, however small that adjustment might turn out to be.The simplest way to use Gates' idea is to become genuinely more deliberate about actively asking for feedback rather than waiting for it to arrive unprompted. At work, instead of simply asking whether a project went well overall, someone can ask a colleague directly what could have actually been clearer or more effective. A student can ask a teacher which specific part of an answer genuinely needs the most work. There is also real value in choosing the right people to ask in the first place. Honest feedback tends to be most useful when it comes from someone who genuinely understands the situation, and who is actually willing to be straightforward with you rather than simply agreeable.Bill Gates' quote is ultimately about something genuinely ordinary, simply allowing other people to show us what we honestly cannot see for ourselves. Real improvement is rarely a single dramatic moment. Far more often, it comes through a series of small corrections made gradually over time, a better explanation offered here, a slightly different approach tried there, a habit finally changed after someone else genuinely pointed it out. The person offering the feedback may only be sharing a few honest sentences. For the person genuinely willing to actually listen, those few sentences can sometimes reveal an entirely different way of looking at the work, the situation, or even themselves.
Article Summary: Bill Gates: "We all need people who will give us feedback. That's how we improve" The Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist made the point in a TED talk. The real story behind this quote is that people need honest feedback from others.

Article Title: Apple shares owner since its IPO days, Florida billionaire buys Ferrari’s first EV, designed by iPhone designer Jony Ive; 87-year-old is 'known for' never selling ...

Long-time Apple share owner Ferrari Luce bought for $40 million

From owning Apple shares to a Jony Ive-designed Ferrari

Ferrari Luce is the company's first electric production car

Florida billionaire and longtime Apple investor Herbert A. Wertheim has paid $40 million for the first production Ferrari Luce, the automaker’s first fully electric production car. The 87-year-old investor bought Apple shares when the company went public in 1980 and is known for holding onto his investments for decades. The Ferrari Luce he bought, has been designed in collaboration with LoveFrom, the creative studio founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive and designer Marc Newson. The car, known as Chassis 0, was sold at an RM Sotheby’s auction in Monterey for more than 36 times its $1.1 million presale estimate.Herbert A. Wertheim bought the first production Ferrari Luce at the RM Sotheby’s Monterey auction. The entire $40 million hammer price will go to the Ferrari Foundation. The car is marked as Chassis 0, giving it a special place in the Luce’s production history. Ferrari’s Tailor Made division also created a unique specification for the vehicle.The car has a one-off Madreperla Semi-Gloss finish that can shift between green and violet depending on the lighting and viewing angle.The interior uses Perla Le Mans metallic leather with Grigio Corvara details.Herbert A. Wertheim's connection with Apple goes back to the company's 1980 IPO. He bought shares when Apple went public and continued building his position over the years. Forbes reported in 2019 that Wertheim owned 1.25 million Apple shares, which were then worth about $195 million. His portfolio has also included companies such as Microsoft, Google, GE, BP and Bank of America.The Ferrari purchase has a connection to Apple's design history because the Luce was created in collaboration with LoveFrom, the design studio founded by Jony Ive after his long career at Apple. Ive played a key role in the design of several major Apple products, including the iPhone and Apple Watch.The Luce is Ferrari's first fully electric production automobile.
